title: Nucleosome Positioning
text: Global gene expression patterns established maintained concerted actions transcription factors (TFs) proteins constitute chromatin. key structural element chromatin nucleosome, consists octameric histone core wrapped 145-147 bp DNA connected neighbor approximately 10-80 bp linker DNA (Polishko et al. 2012). literature nucleosome positioning commonly focuses frequentist inferences within parametric approaches (see instance Chen et al. (2010) Xi et al. (2010)). works, detection nucleosome positions done using hidden Markov model assumed known order. RJMCMCNucleosomes package implementation fully Bayesian hierarchical model profiling nucleosome positions based high-throughput short-read data (MNase-Seq data). implementation based strategy incorporates four aspects. First, jointly models local concentrations directional reads. Second, uses Multinomial-Dirichlet model construction informative prior distribution coupled t-mixture model unknown degrees freedom. Third, number nucleosomes considered random variable refers prior distribution. Fourth, unknown parameters simultaneously estimated using reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) simulation technique (see instance Green (1995) Richardson Green (1997)). Detailed information model can found article mentioned citing section.

text: synthetic nucleosome sample containing 50 nucleosomes (40 well-positioned + 10 fuzzy) created using Bioconductor package nucleoSim. synthetic sample used throughout analysis.
code: ## Load nucleoSim package library(nucleoSim)  val.num       <- 50     ### Number of well-positioned nucleosomes val.del       <- 10     ### Number of well-positioned nucleosomes to delete val.var       <- 30     ### Variance associated to well-positioned nucleosomes val.fuz       <- 10     ### Number of fuzzy nucleosomes val.fuz.var   <- 50     ### Variance associated to fuzzy nucleosomes val.max.cover <- 70     ### Maximum coverage for one nucleosome val.nuc.len   <- 147    ### Nucleosome length val.len.var   <- 10     ### Variance associated to the length of the reads val.lin.len   <- 20     ### The length of the DNA linker val.rnd.seed  <- 100    ### Set seed when result needs to be reproducible val.offset    <- 10000  ### The number of bases used to offset all                          ### nucleosomes and reads  ## Create sample using a Normal distribution sample <- nucleoSim::syntheticNucReadsFromDist(wp.num=val.num,                                     wp.del=val.del, wp.var=val.var,                                     fuz.num=val.fuz, fuz.var=val.fuz.var,                                     max.cover=val.max.cover,                                      nuc.len=val.nuc.len,                                     len.var=val.len.var,                                      lin.len=val.lin.len,                                     rnd.seed=val.rnd.seed,                                     distr="Normal", offset=val.offset)  ## Create visual representation of the synthetic nucleosome sample plot(sample)

text: package detects nucleosome positions genome-wide paired-end single-end MNase-Seq reads using Bayesian hierarchical model. Read positions modelled mixture Student's t-distributions informative Multinomial-Dirichlet prior nucleosome locations, number nucleosomes estimated reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) algorithm. Functions provided split chromosomes segments parallel analysis, merge post-process predictions, plot nucleosome positions alongside read coverage.
